name: Extended Audio Description (Prerecorded)
explanation: This criterion is a stricter, rarer version of SC 1.2.5 Audio Description. Regular audio description squeezes narration into the existing pauses between lines of dialogue. But some videos are so dense with dialogue or fast-moving visuals that there isn't enough silence to fit a description in. This criterion applies to exactly that situation: when the natural pauses are too short, you must pause the video itself, stretching out its running time to make room for the narration, then resume playback once the description finishes. SC 1.2.5 fits description into the video's existing timeline; this criterion lengthens the timeline when that isn't enough. It only applies where standard audio description has already been provided but is still not sufficient.
whoItAffects: Blind users and people with low vision who rely on audio description depend on extended audio description for content where regular description falls short — a fast-paced tutorial with rapid on-screen steps, or a scene with a lot of simultaneous visual action, like a whiteboard being filled in. Without the video pausing to make room, a standard audio description track would either talk over the dialogue or skip important visual detail. This matters most for technical or information-dense video, where missing a visual detail because there wasn't time to describe it means missing something the content depends on.

codeExample.bad:
<!-- Fast-paced software tutorial: constant narration over screen actions leaves no pauses
     long enough to describe rapid UI changes. Only a standard (non-extended) description
     track is offered, so on-screen detail during busy sections is simply dropped. -->
<video controls width="640" height="360">
  <source src="advanced-editing-tutorial.mp4" type="video/mp4">
  <track kind="captions" src="tutorial-en.vtt" srclang="en" label="English">
  <track kind="descriptions" src="tutorial-ad-en.vtt" srclang="en" label="English audio description">
  Your browser does not support the video tag.
</video>
codeExample.good: Watch the standard-length version without extended description.

howToTest: Watch the video with its standard audio description track turned on. Note any moments where the narrator's description feels rushed or cut off, or where something visual is happening but there wasn't time to describe it. If this happens often, check whether the site offers a separate extended audio description version, where the video visibly pauses at those points to let the narration finish. This criterion is not met if the only option is the standard-length track and important visual information is still being dropped.

check.question: A densely-narrated documentary already has a standard audio description track (SC 1.2.5), but the narrator often has to skip visual details because dialogue leaves no pauses long enough to describe them. What does SC 1.2.7 (Extended Audio Description) require in this case?
choices: The video's timeline itself must be paused at those points, extending its total running time, so there is room to describe everything important
Nothing more — providing a standard audio description track already satisfies every audio description requirement
A full text transcript must be linked below the video instead of adding any more audio
The dialogue must be re-recorded to include shorter, faster sentences so descriptions fit in the existing pauses
